items.quote: So, 23 acquisitions have been done in this five-year plan, all following that path, and we have been extremely successful at that. One more thing, Motherson does not buy and sell companies. We buy, we invest, we grow companies. Till date, we have not sold one company from our fold.

items.statement: One large acquisition could be turning point to reach US$ 108 billion target; strong M&A pipeline exists
items.quote: We have an extremely strong pipeline of mergers and acquisitions that will significantly allow us to reach very, very close to that number of 108. Just one big acquisition can be completely turning point for Motherson.

items.statement: SMR grew from 500 million euros to 2.3 billion euros revenue
items.quote: So yeah, truly Vaaman, it has been an incredible journey, going from 500 million euros to 2.3 billion euros now.

items.statement: SMR developed full camera monitoring system (CMS) competence: cameras, hardware, software, algorithms, testing labs, cyber security, OTA updates, functional safety
items.quote: We've been able to develop our own cameras now, we do our hardware, software, algorithms, we have a full testing lab, we do our EMC testing in house, we have an image quality lab in house, we do homologation and we have now in house expertise on cyber security, over the air updates and functional safety.

items.statement: Wiring harness division vertically integrated: connectors, terminals, wires, compounding, stamping, tooling, testing, design engineering
items.quote: Similarly, terminals allowed us to do pressure stamping. Today we are not pressure stamping terminals only in India, but other parts of the world like North America. Not only that, it allowed us to pressure stamp today parts for body in white and not only do cold stamping but also hot stamping, and even big parts like the long members of chassis of the trucks.

items.statement: Supplies to 7 of top 10 Chinese EV manufacturers; positioned to grow with them globally
items.quote: We supplied to seven out of the top ten new electric vehicle manufacturers over there and wherever they go in the world, Of course, we can use those relationships and deepen our penetration with these car makers as well.

items.statement: Honda entrusted Motherson with three supplier companies in Japan, demonstrating deep trust
items.quote: This speaks volumes about the confidence which Honda has in Motherson. And it's not just confidence, it is also trust in terms of how Motherson manages its business, how we treat our customers and the common values that we share.

items.statement: CMS cost delta vs traditional mirrors reduced from 10x to 2.5-3x; expects further reduction with electronics pricing trends
items.quote: When we started this journey, it was about 10x. I would say now it's going down to 2.53x. With and when we all understand how electronics pricing moves so over the years, I think it's going to change and it's going to see traction over there as well.

items.statement: Runs global talent factory programs to develop 'number two' leaders across all levels for Vision 2030
items.quote: While Vishal is building a mega factory, we are building a talent factory across the globe. We have started a numerous number of programs which we all link together to make sure that we have sufficient bandwidth inside the management, not only to the business today, but as well the business which is coming up on our journey to 2030.

items.statement: Policy: never rehire former employees; promote from within; many leaders started in different roles
items.quote: At Motherson, we have a policy, if you leave us, you come back only next life. We do not rehire because it's unfair to our people who've stuck with us. We give our people the opportunity to rise up.

items.statement: Wiring harness division grew nearly as much in last 5 years as in previous 35 years
items.quote: If we see our history in the last five years, we have grown nearly at the same level which we did in the last 35 years of our history in the wiring harness division.

items.statement: SMR delivering much higher than 40% growth for the group
items.quote: A wonderful success story in Motherson that continues to thrive, continues to develop new products, and delivers a much higher growth than 40% for us in the group.

items.statement: Sees record bankruptcies in Europe among developed countries; views as M&A opportunity
items.quote: We're seeing in some of the developed countries a record number of bankruptcies. We have an extremely strong pipeline of mergers and acquisitions that will significantly allow us to reach very, very close to that number of 108.

items.statement: Ambition to assemble full cars for OEMs (Tier 0.5) using just-in-sequence supply chain capability; extends to white goods and consumer electronics
items.quote: Envisage that in this next five-year plan we will get an opportunity to assemble a full car for our customers, for an OEM, and that is our ambition.

items.statement: China footprint: 33 facilities, 13,000 people, 5 strong JV partners across multiple product lines
items.quote: We have 33 facilities doing multiple product lines with all our technologies already there. We have 13,000 talented people already in that region and five very strong joint venture local partners that help us navigate through all the that we have over there to help us solve and partner with us.

items.statement: Vision 2030 gross revenue target of 108 billion USD
items.quote: Of course, you've heard the 108 target in gross revenues. We are going to maintain the 40 % ROCE target for the group.

items.statement: Vision 2030 ROCE target of 40% for the group
items.quote: We are going to maintain the 40 % ROCE target for the group. Of course, all the new businesses are not going to achieve that on day one.

items.statement: Vision 2030 diversification target: no country, customer, or component >10% of revenue
items.quote: In the diversification, we've held strong. No country, no customer, no component to be more than 10% of our revenues.

items.statement: Vision 2030 dividend payout target up to 40% of consolidated profit
items.quote: And we will have the financial discipline to pay out up to 40% of our consolidated profit as dividend throughout this journey

items.statement: Invested over 15,000 crores in last five-year period (Vision 2025)
items.quote: And that's something that I'm really, really proud of. On top of that, as shareholders, I hope we have happy shareholders. We've paid out a record number of dividends. We did not miss a dividend even in the COVID year. We knew that our shareholders needed money at those critical times. We paid that out. We conserved cash, but we made sure that we paid out dividend every single year. And the highes

items.statement: Targets 100% green power for Chennai facility by 2030, not 2035 or 2040
items.quote: The last 25 to 30% will be done by implementing additional renewable capacity with battery energy storage systems, power trading solutions, as well as minimal purchase of green energy attributes to reach 100% green power, not by 2040, not by 2035, but by 2030 for this particular facility.

items.statement: Plans one of world's largest solar rooftop installations on 33 football field sized roof at Chennai facility
items.quote: We have the potential of doing one of the world's largest solar rooftop Installations in the world on this particular roof.

items.statement: Aims to reach USD 108 billion revenue target by 2030 through automotive growth and acquisitions
items.quote: With this slide, what I really wanted to showcase to you is that we mapped out all the different OEMs by region and all of our current products, not doing the not yet products that Motherson is in. And as you can see, there is still significant amounts of headroom for growth in different geographies, different customers, different product lines to hit quite a big number in that 108 target and dent

items.statement: Completed 23 acquisitions in last five-year plan with financial and operational discipline; no divestments
items.quote: If you look at the 23 acquisitions that we have done and of course the 47 or 48 now that was just recently announced acquisitions that we have done, we obviously have to have a very, very strong M&A network and framework in Motherson itself.

items.statement: Acquired three Honda supplier companies in Japan: Yachiyo, Atsumitec, and Yutaka
items.quote: And yet this very same super traditional, super conservative Honda decided to entrust a foreign, a non-Japanese, a gaijin company, Motherson, with not one, not two, but three of their supplier companies. Yes, Yachiyo, Atsumitec, the two names that you see here. And third one is Yutaka, which we just announced a couple of days ago, and we are in the process of closing.

items.statement: SMR grew from EUR 500 million to EUR 2.3 billion revenue since 2009 acquisition
items.quote: So yeah, truly Vaaman, it has been an incredible journey, going from 500 million euros to 2.3 billion euros now.

items.statement: SMR developed full system competency in camera monitoring systems including cameras, hardware, software, algorithms, testing labs, cyber security, and OTA updates
items.quote: We've been able to develop our own cameras now, we do our hardware, software, algorithms, we have a full testing lab, we do our EMC testing in house, we have an image quality lab in house, we do homologation and we have now in house expertise on cyber security, over the air updates and functional safety.

items.statement: Supplies to seven of top ten Chinese EV manufacturers; positioned to grow with them globally
items.quote: We supplied to seven out of the top ten new electric vehicle manufacturers over there and wherever they go in the world, Of course, we can use those relationships and deepen our penetration with these car makers as well.

items.statement: Operates 33 facilities in China with 13,000 employees and five strong JV partners
items.quote: We have 33 facilities doing multiple product lines with all our technologies already there. We have 13,000 talented people already in that region and five very strong joint venture local partners that help us navigate through all the that we have over there to help us solve and partner with us, to help us grow in that region with a local face that can really make sure that Motherson thrives in tha

items.statement: Ambition to assemble full cars for OEMs in next five-year plan as EV transition reduces OEM motivation for in-house assembly
items.quote: Envisage that in this next five-year plan we will get an opportunity to assemble a full car for our customers, for an OEM, and that is our ambition.

items.statement: Runs global talent factory programs to develop internal successors (Number Twos) across all levels for Vision 2030
items.quote: While Vishal is building a mega factory, we are building a talent factory across the globe. We have started a numerous number of programs which we all link together to make sure that we have sufficient bandwidth inside the management, not only to the business today, but as well the business which is coming up on our journey to 2030 that all together creates talents inside the group.

items.statement: Wiring harness division grew nearly as much in last five years as in previous 35 years
items.quote: If we see our history in the last five years, we have grown nearly at the same level which we did in the last 35 years of our history in the wiring harness division.

items.statement: CMS cost delta versus traditional mirrors reduced from 10x to 2.5-3x; expects further reduction with electronics pricing trends
items.quote: When we started this journey, it was about 10x. I would say now it's going down to 2.53x. With and when we all understand how electronics pricing moves so over the years, I think it's going to change and it's going to see traction over there as well.

items.statement: Sees record bankruptcies in Europe creating strong M&A pipeline to reach USD 108 billion target
items.quote: We're seeing in some of the developed countries a record number of bankruptcies. We have an extremely strong pipeline of mergers and acquisitions that will significantly allow us to reach very, very close to that number of 108.

items.statement: Maintains lean overhead with five regional Chairman's offices providing central legal, tax, M&A support to divisions
items.quote: We have five regional offices, we have small number of global functions, which have allowed us to keep the overhead structure extremely lean. And we don't replicate these special functions like legal, Tax, M&A, we don't replicate that in the verticals.

items.statement: Company policy: never rehire former employees; promote from within to build loyalty and growth
items.quote: At Motherson, we have a policy, if you leave us, you come back only next life. We do not rehire because it's unfair to our people who've stuck with us. We give our people the opportunity to rise up.

items.statement: Tega Industries and Apollo Funds entered a term sheet to acquire Molycop for ~$1.48B, expected to close by Dec 31, 2025 or early Jan 2026 subject to regulatory approvals
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that Tega Industries, in partnership with Apollo Funds, as a significant minority investor, has entered into a term sheet to acquire Molycop, a leading global supplier in grinding media for the mining industry, from an affiliate of American Industrial Partners, a private equity firm. The transaction is valued at approximately $1.48 billion and is expected to close by Dec

items.statement: Tega to fund acquisition via $248M equity (preferential allotment and QIP) and $112M debt; promoter family to invest INR150-200 crore in preferential allotment
items.quote: For Tega, the transaction is proposed to be funded through a mix of equity instruments, including preferential allotment and qualified institutional placements, amounting to $248 million, with a debt infusion in Tega of about $112 million. The promoter family plans to take part in the preferential allotment and infuse INR150 crores to INR200 crores.

items.statement: Molycop debt ~$1B to be refinanced down to $780M at close; target net debt/EBITDA <2.5x in 3-4 years; interest cost expected to drop 20-30 bps
items.quote: Molycop's current debt stands at approximately $1 billion. In partnership with Apollo, a financial investor, we plan to co-invest and bring the debt down to $780 million from day one. This reduction is expected to support an upgrade from our existing rating, credit rating, and over the next four years, we aim to lower our net debt to EBITDA ratio to less than 2.5x.

items.statement: Molycop sustenance capex ~$20M/year; growth capex $20-30M over time for high-chrome expansion, funded from internal accruals
items.quote: Not a significant amount of capex, but about, say, $20 million to $30 million of capex infusion may be required over a period of time, which will be mainly done through the internal accruals there. Kirtan Mehta: And what is the sustenance capex levels? Sharad Kumar Khaitan: Sustenance capex level will be close to about $20 million

items.statement: Molycop forged capacity ~1.7M tons at ~70% utilization; high-chrome capacity 20k tons (fully utilized) in Middle East and Indonesia, target 200k tons
items.quote: So, on forged, the capacity is approx. 1.7 million tons. Capacity utilization is at about 70%-odd. In high-chrome, the current capacity is about 20,000 tons and it's fully utilized.

items.statement: Molycop revenue normalized growth ~4.5-5% (forged) and high-chrome growing at ~20% from low base; combined growth ~7.5% over next 3 years
items.quote: Today, forged media is the substantial portion of the revenue. And as explained earlier, while the forged media business will grow at about 5%, the addition of the high-chrome strategy will increase the growth rates to about 7.5% over the next three years.

items.statement: Molycop high-chrome volumes grew from 0 to 62k tons in 2 years; target 200k tons; technology/digital revenue small but targeted to grow 25%+ YoY with margins ~2x core products
items.quote: In the last two years, they've been able to increase high-chrome penetration from 0 to 62,000 tons in the past two years. And the aim is to scale to 200,000 tons for the next.

items.statement: Molycop working capital cycle ~70-80 days; target to maintain at current levels
items.quote: The working capital cycles at Molycop is less than about, it's about 70 to 80 odd days and that's how we want to retain it as of now.

items.statement: US tariffs expected to strengthen position by creating entry barriers; Molycop has local manufacturing in key geographies mitigating anti-dumping risks
items.quote: Given the diversified global footprint of both Tega and Molycop across multiple regions, we see minimal geopolitical risk exposure. In fact, recent US tariffs are expected to strengthen our position in the US market by creating entry barriers, further supporting the domestic growth and competitiveness.

items.statement: Both companies to operate as distinct entities under coordinated leadership; talent retention and cross-functional collaboration prioritized; joint governance for integration
items.quote: While both companies will continue to operate as distinct entities, they will be managed under a coordinated leadership framework to drive synergy and strategic alignment. Talent retention and cross-functional collaboration will be actively supported to preserve institutional knowledge.

items.statement: No direct competitors in technology/digital space for Molycop; high-chrome competition from Magotteaux/AIA in Africa/Australia but Molycop expanding local capacity to compete
items.quote: So, there are certain markets where high-chrome has got greater traction. For example, if you look at Africa and Australia, there has been high-chrome, which has been replacing some of the small size forged media, small and medium, and recognising that these particular markets, high- chrome has had a higher conversion rate, is why Molycop decided to launch its own high-chrome media

items.statement: Capex of INR 400 crores expected in current year and similar amount next year; group CEO announced INR 4,500 crores total investment over next five years up to 2030
items.value: INR 400 crores (current year), INR 4,500 crores (5 years)
items.quote: Well, the current year looks at close to INR 400 crores of capex and almost a similar amount we see next year. However, the group CEO was here. He has clearly announced that the total investment in next five years, up to 2030, will be close to INR 4,500 crores.

items.statement: INR 1,700 crores invested over last three years; incremental sales of INR 2,800 crores generated; localization ratio improved to 79% from ~74%
items.quote: But currently, we are having incremental sales in last three years of INR 2,800 crores. And thereby, the localization ratio has gone up to 79%.

items.statement: Localization ratio inched close to 79% of sales from Indian plants, up from ~74% two to three years ago; non-bearing localization ~90%, bearing localization lower with room to improve
items.quote: And we see this year, so far, the localization ratio has gone up, inching very close to 79%. So, whatever is our sales, 79% of that is coming from our manufacturing plants in India. This ratio just two to three years back used to be around 74%.

items.statement: Portfolio split 60% bearings, 40% non-bearings; non-bearing localization ~90%, bearing localization has further opportunity
items.quote: Because we still have in our total portfolio, 60% is bearings and 40% is non-bearings. In the non-bearing space, localization ratio is close to 90%. But in the bearing space, we have still opportunities to improve the localization ratio further.

items.statement: E-axle complete production line investment estimated at INR 200 crores; phased localization underway with phase two targeting assembly start by mid next year
items.quote: And if we bring the complete line, that line itself would be pretty expensive, like INR 200 crores PUBLIC worth of line. So, which, but for that we need economy of scale, but that has to come by 2030 as the country looks at the EV penetration of close to 15%-20

items.statement: EV adoption in India still under 5% of total vehicles; optimistic adoption seen at 15-20% by 2030-2032; 100% EV far away
items.quote: But nevertheless, the good thing is we are here. So, to be fixated or rigid and say that, look, we only will do a system level offering like e-axle, would not be the right decision as a strategy. So, while we have business wins, we will play the system game, but nothing is stopping us from also playing the component level supplier.

items.statement: Tata Harrier EV business win for e-axle as primary powertrain; integration and testing started at Pune plant; supply channel development with Indian suppliers underway
items.quote: Our primary offering is the e-axle there. And as you must have already seen in the news, the offering is going as a primary powertrain, meaning that's what drives the vehicle. And that's what we offer, and it encompasses the electric motor with the gearbox and the power electronics to manage the performance.

items.statement: India is global hub for cylindrical roller bearings (CRB) including engineering, design, development and manufacturing; significant volumes exported
items.quote: There are portfolios, particularly in our bearings portfolio. Certain range of bearings like the cylindrical roller bearings, India has become the hub globally. Not just from a manufacturing point of view, but from an engineering and design and development point of view as well.

items.statement: Localization and backward integration driving EBITDA margin improvement; localization leads to top-line growth and operating margin improvement
items.quote: And also, you can see that due to localization, the EBITDA margin has gone up. Because within those investments, we have backward integration, land and buildings, a lot of margin improvement projects and relevant investments.

items.statement: Aftermarket viewed as necessary opportunity with good margins in both industrial and automotive; BS VI products now entering aftermarket after 4-5 year lag
items.quote: I would say it's a necessary opportunity for us. Why do I say that? Because the aftermarket presents us with good margin business. Yes. Both in industrial space and in automotive space.

items.statement: Two-wheeler EV strategy: OEMs currently making EV tech in-house (Ola, TVS, Bajaj); Schaeffler ready to supply when market shifts to outsourcing; 2-wheeler exposure 5-6% of overall portfolio
items.quote: What we see is today in the 2-wheeler space, one important difference. Unlike in the passenger cars. And that is every 2-wheeler wants to make their EV technology in-house. Whether it is an Ola, whether it is a TVS, whether it is a Bajaj. Everyone is making their own technology.

items.statement: Vitesco integration complete on business and functional side; operating as one company; recent e-mobility wins (battery management systems) from Vitesco side; 910 engineers at Bangalore R&D center now working for India
items.quote: We are already integrated. We are generating business already as a company because, okay, let me clarify. You know, there are two aspects of the integration. One is on the business side and the functional side. So, we are already working as one company.

items.statement: Capex to be funded entirely from internal generation; no external funding taken historically
items.quote: Investments so far, like last year, I have been with Schaeffler for 34 years and I have never seen Schaeffler taking the external funding to invest. So, it will do from its own generation, that is sure.

items.statement: Asset turnover of 1:2 for finished product capacity investments; localization, land, building, backward integration do not translate to turnover
items.quote: Generally, yes. If it is only towards the capacity. So, one has to be careful. If I am localizing the already traded part, then you will not see that in the top line. And also, if I am making investments for backward integration like roller localization or any other part localization, then you will not see it in the turnover. But generally, the formula is 1 :2. But only for the finished product.

items.statement: Hybrid vehicles expected to reach equal share with EVs in 5-6 years; already supplying planetary gearboxes and other solutions to Japanese OEMs; local production started
items.quote: And so, we believe, our research reports show, I think in the next 5 to 6 years, more or less even hybrids would enjoy equal share of the cake, as much as the EVs would be having. So, more or less.

items.statement: Railways focus on safety, reliability, comfort; Schaeffler strong in reliability and electric locomotive current insulated bearings; Class K bearings approved for Vande Bharat bogies; freight wagon upgrade opportunity
items.quote: What we are seeing in railways is, the railways as a sector is transforming now. Obviously, with all the push from the Indian railways, particularly on three parameters, which they are clearly focusing their growth strategy. Safety, obviously, is one of them. Reliability is the second one. And comfort and convenience is the third.

items.statement: Wind turbine bearings: 80-85% of India production exported; manufacturing up to 4MW turbines locally; gearing up for 6MW+ and larger diameter bearings; offshore 10-15MW potential long-term
items.quote: The second is the stratification in the wind segment as you see. The flagship models used to be in the 2–4-megawatt turbine capacity, which we are seeing now, the demand for beyond 4 PUBLIC beginning to happen. 6 megawatts have started to come in. And all indications are it is likely to go even 9 and beyond as well, okay

items.statement: No steel sourced from China; special steel from Japan and Korea; working with Indian suppliers to meet quality consistency for critical roller/ball components; rings already localized
items.quote: and foremost, we don't buy any steel from China. Questioner: Yes, I know. Harsha Kadam: So, a lot of our steel is sourced in India. Some of it is because of the special category of steel. That's, we get it from Japan, some from Korea. That's it, okay

items.statement: Exports mainly industrial bearings; current year uptick due to lower base (2022 peak INR 1,100 crores); mix: 50% Europe, 10% USA, 40% China/SE Asia; Europe growing 3-4%, SE Asia/Korea targeted for growth; no export revenue target, strategy
items.quote: So, export is mainly bearings for the industrial solutions. And rightfully , because the automotive does not import. Their supply chain is in the country, rather in the city where they are located. PUBLIC So, it is mainly for industrial applications , and it is mainly bearings. And current year's export uptick is actually because we are looking at the lower base last year

items.statement: GST rate cuts on bearings: demand impact delayed due to supply chain confusion near festival season; timing could have been better (two months earlier); no net effect on manufacturer credit/debit
items.quote: But I think it will stabilize. It will take a little bit time as per our opinion. The intention, Diwali, Dhamaka is not happening because still the whole supply chain, the goods which are in pipeline in winter, they are all confused right now.

items.statement: E-clutch, EPS, rear wheel steering in portfolio; commercial vehicle manufacturers showing interest in E-clutch for easier driving; technology ready, awaiting customer demand
items.quote: Yes, surely. That's already in our portfolio. The E-clutch is in our portfolio. EPS is in our portfolio. So, rear wheel steering is in our portfolio. So we have the entire gamut of it. It's about what the Indian market wants, ultimately, okay.

items.statement: No overlap or impact from Continental demerger; Schaeffler has no stake in Continental automotive business
items.quote: I think except for Mr. Schaeffler owning equity into that company, there is nothing much for us at Schaeffler. We have no stake in it. We have absolutely no overlapping, no impact whatsoever.

items.statement: Group e-mobility EBIT losses (EUR 1bn) sit in Germany due to development costs; India e-axle business breaking even in first year; no debt concern at India level
items.quote: We have ensured that it is breaking even in the very first year of its operation. So the e-axle sale that we are doing to Tata is not leading to any negative impacts on us, because the development costs are sitting in Germany.

items.statement: Parent not desperate to leverage India valuation; any future use of India market cap would be for India's inorganic growth; India should reap benefits of its valuation
items.quote: His statement was we are not in that desperate situation. The day we do that; it will be for growth of India. So there will be inorganic growth in India for which, of course, we can do the same.

items.statement: Vitesco Bangalore R&D center has 910 engineers working on global projects (BMW, AMG, Mercedes) and now India projects; recent business wins driven by local design
items.quote: As I am speaking, close to 910 engineers are working there. A lot of work they do for Germany, of course. All the BMWs, the AMGs, the Mercedes. But now they have started to work for India as well.

items.statement: Two-wheeler and off-road together 20-25% of industrial business (40% of total); industrial business 40% of portfolio
items.quote: If you look at within the industrial business, two-wheelers and off-roads put together would be in the range of 20% to 25%, if you look at it on a CY basis.

items.statement: Target 12.2 million tons ore production by FY31 across all mines
items.quote: So, this is the brief projections of this thing. About Khetri I mentioned, we are planning to produce about 1.5 million tons from Khetri and 1.4 million tons from Kolihan. Kolihan will pick up, it is just started I told you in April month.

items.statement: Malanjkhand target 5 million tons ore by FY31
items.quote: The Malajkhand production will reach up to 5 million tons. The Khetri production, which is about 1-1.2 million tons will reach to 2.9 million tons.

items.statement: Jharkhand mines target 4.3 million tons ore by FY31
items.quote: And the ICC mines, which I say Jharkhand or Ghatsila, I'll speak Ghatsila because it is in the locality of Ghatsila only. That will reach up to 4.3,3 million tons will come from Rakha, that is MDO. 0.9 will come from Surda and 0.4 will come from Kendadih mine.

items.statement: FY26 ore production at 85-90% of target due to heavy monsoon
items.quote: And whatever we have, envisaged this year, we are about 85 to 90% of the production of ore. And reason, primarily reason is that we have got huge rainfall this monsoon.

items.statement: Expect to make up production shortfall in Q3 and Q4 FY26
items.quote: So that was the loss, which we expect to make up not in 2nd quarter but in the 3rd quarter. Because 2nd quarter you have seen that still heavy rains have continued.

items.statement: Malanjkhand capex ~Rs 900 crore for shafts equipping, concentrator, crusher, ventilation
items.quote: Malanjkhand we will install crusher. Two shafts, concentrator plant, ventilation fans, substation, electricity panel, crusher, etc will be required.

items.statement: Khetri and Jharkhand capex ~Rs 200 crore each for augmentation
items.quote: Khetri and Jharkhand if you take 200 each and 900 in Malanjkhand then 1300 crore is presently required apart from other CAPEX.

items.statement: Rakha mine capex Rs 2,600-2,700 crore by MDO over 6-7 years, no HCL capex
items.quote: Approx 26-2700 crore investment will be done over a period of 6-7 years by South West mining which is a company of JSW.

items.statement: Annual mine development capex ~Rs 150 crore for underground development
items.quote: There is a development capex of the underground mines every year. So, it is around 150 crores, which we incur regularly for making new development of the mines and then going for the production.

items.statement: Malanjkhand shafts sunk, equipping to take 30-32 months after tender award
items.quote: After the tender is awarded, it will take 30-32 months to furnish the shafts.

items.statement: Malanjkhand exit run rate 5 million tons by FY31, ramp up via 3.5 mtpa from roads then shaft commissioning
items.quote: Maybe 2028, 2028-29 onwards, basically it is from 2.9 it might go up to 3.5, then 3.8, 4, 4.3, then it will go up to 5. So at least by 2031 we are going to see 5 million tons from Malanjkhand.

items.statement: Khetri target 2.9 million tons (1.5 Khetri + 1.4 Kolihan) by FY31
items.quote: Khetri will remain 1.5, Kolihan 1.4.

items.statement: Jharkhand Surda 0.9 mtpa, Kendadih 0.4 mtpa, Rakha 3 mtpa by FY31
items.quote: 3 million tons will come from Rakha, that is MDO. 0.9 will come from Surda and 0.4 will come from Kendadih mine.

items.statement: Rakha production start within 16-18 months from lease signing
items.quote: We are targeting 16 to 18 months from the lease date, they should start some production from Rakha.

items.statement: Kendadih lease signing within 10-15 days, production start 15-20 days after
items.quote: Within 10 to 15 days, this is the assurance which we have got from the district administration, the Kendadih lease will also be signed. And within 15-20 days, we should start the production and all mining operations in Kendadih also.

items.statement: MIC production target 30,000 tons FY26 (20,000 from Malanjkhand)
items.quote: This year we are expecting 30,000 MIC approx. out of which 20,000 MIC should come from Malanjkhand.

items.statement: MIC production 25,000 tons FY25, 27,000 tons FY24
items.quote: Last year it was 25,000, last to last year, it was 27,000.

items.statement: MIC target 80,000-90,000 tons at 12 million tons ore with 0.7-0.8% grade
items.quote: If the grade is low 90000- 95000, it will be 80,000 to 90,000 tons. Yes, yes. 80,000 to 90,000 tons, MIC will be made.

items.statement: Malanjkhand cost of production ~$5,000/ton MIC inclusive of all costs
items.quote: So, the cost of the Malanjkhand mine is around $5,000 per ton, which is a very competitive price. Very competitive.

items.statement: Khetri cost of production ~$6,000/ton MIC inclusive of all costs
items.quote: So, in Khetri, it is roughly $6,000 per ton. Sorry, dollars per ton.

items.statement: Jharkhand mines cost of production ~$6,000/ton MIC
items.quote: In Jharkhand, there will be around 6,000. That is already an underground mine. All of them will be underground.

items.statement: TCRC currently negative, HCL getting better than LME price on spot basis
items.quote: TCRC is running negative, you may be knowing. So, we are getting better price than the LME.

items.statement: MIC pricing formula LME minus TCRC, currently spot based, vendors requesting annual contracts
items.quote: Our vendors are requesting us to convert it to annual contracts. But now it is on spot.

items.statement: All concentrate sold domestically to Hindalco, Adani, Vedanta; no exports currently
items.quote: India needs concentrate. They were not taking because we had to export. It was compulsion because of low percentage of copper. We were exporting because traders used to come and take it.

items.statement: Rakha EC received 10 days ago, Kendadih EC received 2-3 days ago, lease deeds imminent
items.quote: EC of Rakha received some 10 days ago, EC of Kendadih received some 2-3 days ago. Rakha MDO lease is to be signed today evening or maybe tomorrow morning.

items.statement: All existing mining leases valid for 20 years till 2040-41
items.quote: All existing leases are valid for 20 years till 2040-41. One is 40 another is 42, dates are different.

items.statement: Codelco G2G agreement signed April 1 for technical collaboration, teams visiting in October
items.quote: That is a historic agreement. It took place in front of our Honourable Prime Minister's Hyderabad house on 1st April. I feel proud that Secretary, Mines and I both were invited for the dinner at Rashtrapati Bhawan in the evening along the Chilean team.

items.statement: Employee cost ~Rs 300 crore + Rs 300 crore depreciation; headcount to grow with production but inverted pyramid structure
items.quote: Sir, if you look at approximately 300 crores is the employee cost. Sir, 300 crores depreciation amortisation is done. That's it.

items.statement: Geological risks: dikes in Malanjkhand cause stoppages, grade uncertainty until definition drilling
items.quote: In Malanjkhand, there is a dike. A lot of dikes pass through there. A dike is an unconformity which hinders. When it falls, your work is stopped for 2 days, 2 weeks, 10 days, 5 days, and then the girders are installed.

items.statement: Monsoon seepage impacts underground production, heavy rains in May reduced FY26 output
items.quote: Because of the monsoon. Because of the rains. So, if all that is clear, then we will try to reach there. We will try our best.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated revenue guidance of INR110-130 crores
items.quote: I'm expecting to close this year by INR110 to INR130 crores topline.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of INR200+ crores
items.quote: And then next year, I'm expecting about 200 plus odd numbers, the top line.

items.statement: Consolidated order book of INR56-60 crores EPC standalone, INR18-36 crores from subsidiary, INR35 crores operating revenue
items.quote: About INR56 to INR60 crores on standalone we have the order booking of EPC. About INR30 crores is our operating revenue. About INR18 crores or maybe INR36 crores will be from the subsidiary, that is the order booking.

items.statement: Oman order book of INR20-22 crores
items.quote: So, as of now, if you ask me a number, I can say about INR20 crores - INR22 crores of Indian rupees is the order booking in Oman.

items.statement: Two BOT plants in food sector, INR15 crores and INR20 crores each, total INR35 crores, commissioning by January-February
items.quote: I think INR15 crores for one and INR20 crores for the other. So, I think about INR35 crores.

items.statement: Oman Phase 2 expansion expected to start by December-January, completion this financial year
items.quote: I'm expecting that it was expected to be starting in this September. Somehow, we are getting delayed in day-to-day operations and all. So, I think by December or January, we should be in position to start the Phase 2.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target 26-28%, PAT margin 20-23%
items.quote: Generally what we try to do is we try to touch EBITDA range of about 26% to 28% or somewhere around it. And because of this EBITDA, the PAT is variably in the range of about, let us assume 20% or something, 21% to maybe 23%.

items.statement: Operating revenue higher margin than EPC
items.quote: No, no. So, EPCs are never the higher margin business. Operating revenue is always the higher margin business because it involves a lot of manpower, a lot of service revenue and a lot of day-to-day activities.

items.statement: Oman margins expected to improve due to currency difference and precision work
items.quote: Yes. Yes. It is expected. Yes. Definitely, it is expected because the currency difference is very high compared to India, and it is quite a precision job.

items.statement: Oman Phase 1 current monthly revenue INR2-2.5 crores, Phase 2 to reach INR6-7 crores monthly
items.quote: it is in the range of monthly INR2 crores to INR2.5 crores per month. Devender Bindal: Okay. Ritesh Patel: As soon as we complete these Phase 2 operations as part of, it should reach to about INR6 crores to INR7 crores a month

items.statement: Operating revenue from water plants INR30-35 crores FY26, INR50-60 crores FY27, total capital deployed INR50 crores
items.quote: Operating revenue only on the water side should be about INR30 crores to INR35 crores this year, and should be about INR50 crores to INR60 crores next year, I mean, after this March. And so on, so it will be.

items.statement: Expanding into municipal and smart city projects for wastewater treatment
items.quote: Yes. Of course, we will be expanding in all the ways. But in no chance we are doing a generalized business. Of course, every business will be a specialized business, which will include a lot of engineering and a lot of process part. But yes, as and when the volumes are increasing, so infrastructure development will be our primary target.

items.statement: Oman raw material sourced from multiple refineries (OQ, PDO, OQ8) via government registration and contracts
items.quote: Since we are a registered service provider in the government, Ministry of Environment, all the large oil processing units are being informed by the government about our facilities. So, one-on-one, we try to reach each facility of Oman.

items.statement: Receivables 150-160 days due to project milestone invoicing, considered normal cycle
items.quote: Generally what happens is, specifically, on case-to-case, of course, we can discuss, but generally what happens is, these are projects on a very sizable scale. So, what happens is, some part loads are being dispatched, the invoices are being created, the project is not yet finished, the cycle is not yet completed.

items.statement: No equity raise needed for next year, may explore debt options for expansion
items.quote: So, as of now, the equity part is completed. I do not think we will need any further equity raising in next maybe a year or so. Of course, there are a lot of ways or a lot of options on the debt side which is still open with the company.

items.statement: Internal accruals strong, no external capital needed for at least 1 year
items.quote: So, as of now -- so as of now -- Yes. Yes. Since we've already started generating good cash, so internal accruals are quite strong and that is why I don't foresee any further capital increasement at least up to next 1-year.

items.statement: Headcount 521 employees as of last month
items.quote: Overall, if we say the headcount of staff or the employees who are working day and night for the company has gone to up to 521 as per the last month's record.

items.statement: Oman plant IRR expectation 24-26 months for BOT projects
items.quote: s the IRR? Maybe we can expect 2 to 3 years as a common IRR number for any project. Devender Bindal: Okay. Ritesh Patel: 24 – 26 months to be precise

items.statement: Plan to migrate from SME to NSE main board after March 2026
items.quote: Yes. Maybe, maybe after this March, I mean, this current year March, next year we will be commissioned to, to shift ourselves on the main board.

items.statement: Green Hydrogen plant commissioned for captive consumption, not for sale
items.quote: It is commissioned. Charanjeev Singh: Okay. Ritesh Patel: It is very well commissioned. So, it is for captive consumption. It is not for sale or something

items.statement: No current delays or compliance issues at Oman plant, initial delays resolved
items.quote: So, as of now, there is no delay. As of now, there are no complaint or something. 100% the company is compliant. 100% everything is at place. So, for now, there is no delay.

items.statement: Subsidiary structure with 15-49% minority partners for operational management, no plan to consolidate fully
items.quote: It is not complex. Let me explain you. I am an engineer. I have my own set of people. I have my own team of people who network on the development of the processes or development of the technology. So, I will always need, or we will always need people with team or people with fields of management to operate these companies, to control manpower, to handle manpower, to operate these systems.

items.statement: Oman revenue expected to be 40-50% of consolidated FY27 revenue
items.quote: So, I believe Oman should have about, I think, maybe 50% of our total number should be Oman, I believe. Deepak Poddar: No, no, 80% of what? 80% of total number means? Ritesh Patel: 40% of the total number. Maybe if I'm expecting about 200 plus odd numbers, Oman should be around, what, 60 something

items.statement: Oman revenue variable based on waste quantity processed, sold at market price
items.quote: Now, the total revenue -- these are all approximate numbers. So, total revenue is depending on the quantity of the waste generated and treated and multiplied by the quantity of the waste processed by our plant. So, it is always a little bit variable, but it doesn't impact much on the actual numbers.

items.statement: Quarterly reporting adopted for transparency, will continue
items.quote: Of course. We are trying to get very strong on the compliance part. It was, of course, very comfortable for us to keep it on 6 month basis, but we intentionally did a 3 month data sharing so that everybody knows what is going on. We want to be very transparent with our shareholders.
